Great! Here are minimal, runnable examples to get your first trace into Langfuse.

Python (SDK v4)

  • Install: pip install langfuse

  • Set env (e.g., .env): LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-... LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-... LANGFUSE_BASE_URL=https://cloud.langfuse.com

  • Code: from langfuse import get_client

    langfuse = get_client()

    with langfuse.start_as_current_observation(as_type="span", name="process-request") as span: span.update(output="Processing complete") with langfuse.start_as_current_observation( as_type="generation", name="llm-response", model="gpt-3.5-turbo" ) as gen: gen.update(output="Generated response")

    langfuse.flush() # important for short-lived scripts

Docs:

  • SDK Quickstart (Python): https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/sdk/overview
  • Instrumentation: https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/sdk/instrumentation

JavaScript/TypeScript (SDK v5)

  • Install: npm install @langfuse/tracing @langfuse/otel @opentelemetry/sdk-node

  • Set env (e.g., .env): LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-... LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-... LANGFUSE_BASE_URL=https://cloud.langfuse.com

  • instrumentation.ts: import { NodeSDK } from "@opentelemetry/sdk-node"; import { LangfuseSpanProcessor } from "@langfuse/otel";

    export const sdk = new NodeSDK({ spanProcessors: [new LangfuseSpanProcessor()], }); sdk.start();

  • index.ts: import { sdk } from "./instrumentation"; import { startActiveObservation } from "@langfuse/tracing";

    async function main() { await startActiveObservation("my-first-trace", async (span) => { span.update({ input: "Hello, Langfuse!", output: "This is my first trace!" }); }); }

    main().finally(() => sdk.shutdown()); // flush in short-lived apps

Docs:

  • SDK Quickstart (JS/TS): https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/sdk/overview#quickstart
  • Instrumentation: https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/sdk/instrumentation

Python (SDK v4)

  • Install: pip install langfuse

  • Set env (e.g., .env): LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-... LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-... LANGFUSE_BASE_URL=https://cloud.langfuse.com

  • Code: from langfuse import get_client

    langfuse = get_client()

    with langfuse.start_as_current_observation(as_type="span", name="process-request") as span: span.update(output="Processing complete") with langfuse.start_as_current_observation( as_type="generation", name="llm-response", model="gpt-3.5-turbo" ) as gen: gen.update(output="Generated response")

    langfuse.flush() # important for short-lived scripts

Docs:

  • Instrumentation: https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/sdk/instrumentation

JavaScript/TypeScript (SDK v5)

    async function main() { await startActiveObservation("my-first-trace", async (span) => { span.update({ input: "Hello, Langfuse!", output: "This is my first trace!" }); }); }

    main().finally(() => sdk.shutdown()); // flush in short-lived apps

{"type": "text", "text": "# Langfuse\n\n> Langfuse is an **open-source AI engineering platform** ([GitHub](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse)) that helps teams collaboratively debug, analyze, and iterate on their LLM applications. All platform features are natively integrated to accelerate the development workflow.\n\n## Markdown Access\n\nEvery page on langfuse.com is available as plain Markdown. Append `.md` to any URL, or send an `Accept: text/markdown` header:\n\n```bash\ncurl https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/get-started.md\n```\n\nThe links in the section indexes below already point at the `.md` variants.\n\n## Docs Search API\n\nSemantic search (RAG) over the Langfuse documentation, returning an answer with the relevant pages and excerpts. No authentication required. Use this instead of guessing when a specific page does not answer the question:\n\n```bash\ncurl -sG \"https://langfuse.com/api/search-docs\" --data-urlencode \"query=How do I trace a LangGraph agent?\"\n```\n\n- **Endpoint**: `https://langfuse.com/api/search-docs?query=<question>`\n- **Documentation**: [REST endpoint](https://langfuse.com/docs/docs-mcp#rest-endpoint)\n\nAsk specific, self-contained questions in natural language. This is the same search that backs the `searchLangfuseDocs` MCP tool below.\n\n## Langfuse Docs MCP Server\n\nConnect to the Langfuse Docs MCP server to access documentation directly in your AI editor:\n\n- **Endpoint**: `https://langfuse.com/api/mcp`\n- **Transport**: `streamableHttp`\n- **Documentation**: [Langfuse Docs MCP Server](https://langfuse.com/docs/docs-mcp)\n\nThe MCP server provides tools to search Langfuse documentation, GitHub issues, and discussions. See the [installation guide](https://langfuse.com/docs/docs-mcp) for setup instructions in Cursor, VS Code, Claude Desktop, and other MCP clients.\n\n## Langfuse Skill for AI Coding Agents\n\nInstall the Langfuse skill before implementing anything with Langfuse. The skill provides up-to-date documentation, best-practice workflows for instrumentation, prompt management, and programmatic API access via the Langfuse CLI.\n\nInstall from: [github.com/langfuse/skills](https://github.com/langfuse/skills/tree/main/skills/langfuse)\n\n## Tracing Best Practices\n\nBefore instrumenting an application with Langfuse, read [What does a good {"type": "text", "text": "{\"content\": [{\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/features/trace-ids-and-distributed-tracing\", \"title\": \"Trace IDs & Distributed Tracing\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Trace IDs & Distributed Tracing - Langfuse\\n[Docs](/docs)\\n[Observability](/docs/observability/overview)\\n[Features](/docs/observability/features/sessions)\\n[Trace IDs & Distributed Tracing](/docs/observability/features/trace-ids-and-distributed-tracing)\\n# Trace IDs & Distributed Tracing\\nA **trace ID** is a unique identifier that follows a request as it flows through your system. In distributed systems, trace IDs enable you to correlate operations across multiple services and reconstruct the full request lifecycle.\\nBy default, Langfuse assigns random 32 hexchar trace IDs and 16 hexchar observation IDs.\\n## Creating and accessing Trace IDs\\nPython SDKJS/TS SDK\\nUse [`create_trace_id()`](https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse#Langfuse.create_trace_id) to generate a trace ID. If a `seed` is provided, the ID is deterministic. Use the same seed to get the same ID. This is useful for correlating external IDs with Langfuse traces.\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client, Langfuse\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\nexternal_request_id = \\\"req_12345\\\"\\ndeterministic_trace_id = langfuse.create_trace_id(seed=external_request_id)\\n```\\nUse [`get_current_trace_id()`](https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse#Langfuse.get_current_trace_id) to get the current trace ID and [`get_current_observation_id`](https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse#Langfuse.get_current_observation_id) to get the current observation ID.\\nYou can also use `observation.trace_id` and `observation.id` to access the trace and observation IDs directly from a LangfuseSpan or LangfuseGeneration object.\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client, Langfuse\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\nwith langfuse.start_as_current_observation(as_type=\\\"span\\\", name=\\\"my-op\\\") as current_op:\\n trace_id = langfuse.get_current_trace_id()\\n observation_id = langfuse.get_current_observation_id()\\n print(trace_id, observation_id)\\n```\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nUse [`createTraceId`](https://langfuse-js-git-main-langfuse.vercel.app/functions/_langfuse_tracing.createTraceId.html) to generate a deterministic trace ID from a seed.\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { createTraceId, startObservation } from \\\"@langfuse/tracing\\\";\\nconst externalId = \\\"support-ticket-54321\\\";\\nconst langfuseTraceId = await createTraceId(externalId);\\n```\\nUse [`getActiveTraceId`](https://langfuse-js-git-main-langfuse.vercel.app/functions/_langfuse_tracing.getActiveTraceId.html) to get the active trace ID and [`getActiveSpanId`](https://langfuse-js-git-main-langfuse.vercel.app/functions/_langfuse_tracing.getActiveSpanId.html) to get the current observation ID.\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { startObservation, getActiveTraceId } from \\\"@langfuse/tracing\\\";\\nawait startObservation(\\\"run\\\", async (span) => {\\n const traceId = getActiveTraceId();\\n console.log(`Current trace ID: ${traceId}`);\\n});\\n```\\n## Setting a custom Trace ID\\nYou can set a custom trace ID when wrapping your application code with the Langfuse SDK.\\nPython SDKJS/TS SDK\\n **Using the Context Manager**\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\n///# Use a predefined trace ID with trace_context parameter\\nwith langfuse.start_as_current_observation(\\n as_type=\\\"span\\\",\\n name=\\\"my-operation\\\",\\n trace_context={\\n \\\"trace_id\\\": \\\"abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890\\\", ///# Must be 32 hex chars\\n \\\"parent_span_id\\\": \\\"fedcba0987654321\\\" # Optional, 16 hex chars\\n }\\n) as observation:\\n print(f\\\"This observation has trace_id: {observation.trace_id}\\\")\\n # YOUR APPLICATION CODE HERE\\n```\\n **Using the Decorator**\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import observe\\n@observe()\\ndef my_operation(input):\\n # YOUR APPLICATION CODE HERE\\n result = call_llm(input)\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n return result\\nprocess_user_request(\\n input=\\\"Hello\\\",\\n langfuse_trace_id=\\\"abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890\\\" # Must be 32 hex chars\\n)\\n```\\n **Deterministic trace IDs**\\nWhen starting a new trace with a predetermined `traceId`, you must also provide an arbitrary parent-`spanId` for the parent observation. The parent span ID value is irrelevant as long as it is a valid 16-hexchar string as the span does not actually exist within the trace but is only used for trace ID inheritance of the created observation.\\nYou can create valid, deterministic trace IDs from a seed string using `createTraceId`. This is useful for correlating Langfuse traces with IDs from external systems, like a support ticket ID.\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { createTraceId, startObservation } from \\\"@langfuse/tracing\\\";\\nconst externalId = \\\"support-ticket-54321\\\";\\n// Generate a valid, deterministic traceId from the external ID\\nconst langfuseTraceId = await createTraceId(externalId);\\n// You can now start a new trace with this ID\\nconst rootSpan = startObservation(\\n \\\"process-ticket\\\",\\n {},\\n {\\n parentSpanContext: {\\n traceId: langfuseTraceId,\\n spanId: \\\"0123456789abcdef\\\", // A valid 16 hexchar string; value is irrelevant as parent span does not exist but only used for inheritance\\n traceFlags: 1, // mark trace as sampled\\n },\\n }\\n);\\n// Later, you can regenerate the same traceId to score or retrieve the trace\\nconst scoringTraceId = await createTraceId(externalId);\\n// scoringTraceId will be the same as langfuseTraceId\\n```\\nSetting a parentSpanContext will detach the created span from the active span context as it no longer inherits from the current active span in the context.\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nLearn more in the [Langfuse SDK instrumentation docs](/docs/observability/sdk/instrumentation#trace-ids).\\n* * *\\n* * *\\nLast edited 5/18/2026\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/sdk/instrumentation\", \"title\": \"Instrumentation\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Instrumentation - Langfuse\\n[Docs](/docs)\\n[Observability](/docs/observability/overview)\\n[SDKs](/docs/observability/sdk/overview)\\n[Instrumentation](/docs/observability/sdk/instrumentation)\\n# Instrumentation\\nThere are two main ways to instrument your application with the Langfuse SDKs:\\n * Using our **[native integrations](/integrations)** for popular LLM and agent libraries such as OpenAI, LangChain or the Vercel AI SDK. They automatically create observations and traces and capture prompts, responses, usage, and errors.\\n * Manually instrumenting your application with the Langfuse SDK. The SDKs provide 3 ways to create observations: \\n * **Context manager**\\n * **Observe wrapper**\\n * **Manual observations**\\nAll approaches are interoperable. You can nest a decorator-created observation inside a context manager or mix manual spans with our [native integrations](/integrations).\\n## Custom instrumentation\\nInstrument your application with the Langfuse SDK using the following methods:\\n### Context manager\\nThe context manager allows you to create a new span and set it as the currently active observation in the OTel context for its duration. All new observations created within this block will automatically be its children.\\nPython SDKJS/TS SDK\\n[`start_as_current_observation()`](https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse#Langfuse.start_as_current_observation) is the primary way to create observations while ensuring the active OpenTelemetry context is updated. Any child observations created inside the `with` block inherit the parent automatically.\\nObservations can have different [types](/docs/observability/features/observation-types) by setting the `as_type` parameter.\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client, propagate_attributes\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\nwith langfuse.start_as_current_observation(\\n as_type=\\\"span\\\",\\n name=\\\"user-request-pipeline\\\",\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n// Create a nested span for, e.g., a tool call\\nconst toolCall = span.startObservation(\\n // name\\n \\\"fetch-weather\\\",\\n // params\\n {\\n input: { city: \\\"Paris\\\" },\\n },\\n // Specify observation type in asType\\n // This will type the attributes argument accordingly\\n // Default is 'span'\\n { asType: \\\"tool\\\" }\\n);\\n// Simulate work and end the tool call span\\nawait new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 100));\\ntoolCall.update({ output: { temperature: \\\"15°C\\\" } }).end();\\n// Create a nested generation for the LLM call\\nconst generation = span.startObservation(\\n \\\"llm-call\\\",\\n {\\n model: \\\"gpt-4\\\",\\n input: [{ role: \\\"user\\\", content: \\\"What is the capital of France?\\\" }],\\n },\\n { asType: \\\"generation\\\" }\\n);\\ngeneration.update({\\n usageDetails: { input: 10, output: 5 },\\n output: { content: \\\"The capital of France is Paris.\\\" },\\n});\\ngeneration.end();\\n// End the root span\\nspan.update({ output: \\\"Successfully answered user request.\\\" }).end();\\n```\\nManual Ending Required\\nIf you use [`startObservation()`](https://langfuse-js-git-main-langfuse.vercel.app/functions/_langfuse_tracing.startObservation.html), you are responsible for calling [`.end()`](https://langfuse-js-git-main-langfuse.vercel.app/classes/_langfuse_tracing.LangfuseSpan.html#end) on the returned observation object. Failure to do so will result in incomplete or missing observations in Langfuse.\\n## Nesting observations\\nThe Langfuse SDKs methods automatically handle the nesting of observations.\\nPython SDKJS/TS SDK\\n **Observe Decorator**\\nIf you use the observe wrapper, the function call hierarchy is automatically captured and reflected in the trace.\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import observe\\n@observe\\ndef my_data_processing_function(data, parameter):\\n # ... processing logic ...\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n return {\\\"processed_data\\\": data, \\\"status\\\": \\\"ok\\\"}\\n@observe\\ndef main_function(data, parameter):\\n return my_data_processing_function(data, parameter)\\n```\\n **Context Manager**\\nIf you use the context manager, nesting is handled automatically by OpenTelemetry's context propagation. When you create a new observation using [`start_as_current_observation()`](https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse#Langfuse.start_as_current_observation), it becomes a child of the observation that was active in the context when it was created.\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\nwith langfuse.start_as_current_observation(as_type=\\\"span\\\", name=\\\"outer-process\\\") as outer_span:\\n # outer_span is active\\n with langfuse.start_as_current_observation(as_type=\\\"generation\\\", name=\\\"llm-step-1\\\") as gen1:\\n # gen1 is active, child of outer_span\\n gen1.update(output=\\\"LLM 1 output\\\")\\n with outer_span.start_as_current_observation(name=\\\"intermediate-step\\\") as mid_span:\\n # mid_span is active, also a child of outer_span\\n # This demonstrates using the yielded span object to create children\\n with mid_span.start_as_current_observation(as_type=\\\"generation\\\", name=\\\"llm-step-2\\\") as gen2:\\n # gen2 is active, child of mid_span\\n gen2.update(output=\\\"LLM 2 output\\\")\\n mid_span.update(output=\\\"Intermediate processing done\\\")\\n outer_span.update(output=\\\"Outer process finished\\\")\\n```\\n **Manual Observations**\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nIf you are creating observations manually, you can use the methods on the parent [`LangfuseSpan`](https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse#LangfuseSpan) or [`LangfuseGeneration`](https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse#LangfuseGeneration) object to create children. These children will _not_ become the current context unless their `_as_current_` variants are used (see context manager).\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\nparent = langfuse.start_observation(name=\\\"manual-parent\\\")\\nchild_span = parent.start_observation(name=\\\"manual-child-span\\\")\\n///# ... work ...\\nchild_span.end()\\nchild_gen = parent.start_observation(name=\\\"manual-child-generation\\\", as_type=\\\"generation\\\")\\n///# ... work ...\\nchild_gen.end()\\nparent.end()\\n```\\nNesting happens automatically via OpenTelemetry context propagation. When you create a new observation with [`startActiveObservation`](https://langfuse-js-git-main-langfuse.vercel.app/functions/_langfuse_tracing.startActiveObservation.html), it becomes a child of whatever was active at the time.\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { startActiveObservation } from \\\"@langfuse/tracing\\\";\\nawait startActiveObservation(\\\"outer-process\\\", async () => {\\n await startActiveObservation(\\\"llm-step-1\\\", async (span) => {\\n span.update({ output: \\\"LLM 1 output\\\" });\\n });\\n await startActiveObservation(\\\"intermediate-step\\\", async (span) => {\\n await startActiveObservation(\\\"llm-step-2\\\", async (child) => {\\n child.update({ output: \\\"LLM 2 output\\\" });\\n });\\n span.update({ output: \\\"Intermediate processing done\\\" });\\n });\\n});\\n```\\n## Update observations\\nYou can update observations with new information as your code executes.\\nPython SDKJS/TS SDK\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n with propagate_attributes(\\n user_id=user_id,\\n session_id=session_id,\\n metadata={\\\"pipeline\\\": \\\"main\\\"}\\n ):\\n # All nested @observe functions inherit these attributes\\n result = call_llm()\\n return result\\n@observe()\\ndef call_llm():\\n # This automatically has user_id, session_id, metadata from parent\\n pass\\n```\\nUse [`propagateAttributes()`](https://langfuse-js-git-main-langfuse.vercel.app/functions/_langfuse_tracing.propagateAttributes.html) to add attributes to observations.\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { startActiveObservation, propagateAttributes, startObservation } from \\\"@langfuse/tracing\\\";\\nawait startActiveObservation(\\\"user-workflow\\\", async () => {\\n await propagateAttributes(\\n {\\n userId: \\\"user_123\\\",\\n sessionId: \\\"session_abc\\\",\\n metadata: { experiment: \\\"variant_a\\\", env: \\\"prod\\\" },\\n version: \\\"1.0\\\",\\n traceName: \\\"user-workflow\\\",\\n },\\n async () => {\\n const generation = startObservation(\\\"llm-call\\\", { model: \\\"gpt-4\\\" }, { asType: \\\"generation\\\" });\\n generation.end();\\n }\\n );\\n});\\n```\\nNote on Attribute Propagation\\nWe use Attribute Propagation to propagate specific attributes (userId, sessionId, version, tags, metadata, traceName) across all observations in an execution context. We will use all observations with these attributes to calculate attribute-level metrics. Please consider the following when using Attribute Propagation:\\n * Values must be **strings ≤200 characters**\\n * Metadata keys: **Alphanumeric characters only** (no whitespace or special characters)\\n * Call **early in your trace** to ensure all observations are covered. This way you make sure that all Metrics in Langfuse are accurate.\\n * Invalid values are dropped with a warning\\n### Cross-service propagation\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nFor distributed tracing across multiple services, use the `as_baggage` parameter (see [OpenTelemetry documentation for more details](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/signals/baggage/)) to propagate attributes via HTTP headers.\\nIn the Python SDK, `environment` can also be propagated this way. The environment is sent as `langfuse_environment` baggage and takes precedence over the downstream service's local `LANGFUSE_TRACING_ENVIRONMENT` or client-level environment for spans created within the propagated context.\\nPython SDKJS/TS SDK\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client, propagate_attributes\\nimport requests\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\nwith langfuse.start_as_current_observation(as_type=\\\"span\\\", name=\\\"api-request\\\"):\\n with propagate_attributes(\\n user_id=\\\"user_123\\\",\\n session_id=\\\"session_abc\\\",\\n environment=\\\"staging\\\",\\n as_baggage=True,\\n ):\\n requests.get(\\\"https://service-b.example.com/api\\\")\\n```\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { propagateAttributes, startActiveObservation } from \\\"@langfuse/tracing\\\";\\nawait startActiveObservation(\\\"api-request\\\", async () => {\\n await propagateAttributes(\\n {\\n userId: \\\"user_123\\\",\\n sessionId: \\\"session_abc\\\",\\n asBaggage: true,\\n },\\n async () => {\\n await fetch(\\\"https://service-b.example.com/api\\\");\\n }\\n );\\n});\\n```\\n**Security Warning** : When baggage propagation is enabled, attributes are added to **all** outbound HTTP headers. Only use it for non-sensitive values needed for distributed tracing.\\n## Update trace\\nBy default, trace input/output mirror whatever you set on the **root observation** , the first observation in your trace. You can customize the trace level information if you need to for LLM-as-a-Judge, AB-tests, or UI clarity.\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n[LLM-as-a-Judge](/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/llm-as-a-judge) workflows in Langfuse might rely on trace-level inputs/outputs. Make sure to set them deliberately rather than relying on the root observation if your evaluation payload differs.\\nPython SDKJS/TS SDK\\n **Default Behavior**\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\n///# Using the context manager\\nwith langfuse.start_as_current_observation(\\n as_type=\\\"span\\\",\\n name=\\\"user-request\\\",\\n input={\\\"query\\\": \\\"What is the capital of France?\\\"} ///# This becomes the trace input\\n) as root_span:\\n with langfuse.start_as_current_observation(\\n as_type=\\\"generation\\\",\\n name=\\\"llm-call\\\",\\n model=\\\"gpt-4o\\\",\\n input={\\\"messages\\\": [{\\\"role\\\": \\\"user\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"What is the capital of France?\\\"}]}\\n ) as gen:\\n response = \\\"Paris is the capital of France.\\\"\\n gen.update(output=response)\\n # LLM generation input/output are separate from trace input/output\\n root_span.update(output={\\\"answer\\\": \\\"Paris\\\"}) ///# This becomes the trace output\\n```\\n **Override Default Behavior**\\nUse [`observation.set_trace_io()`](https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse#LangfuseEvent.set_trace_io) or [`langfuse.set_current_trace_io()`](https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse#Langfuse.set_current_trace_io) if you need different trace inputs/outputs than the root observation:\\n`set_trace_io()` and `set_current_trace_io()` are deprecated and exist only for backward compatibility with trace-level LLM-as-a-judge evaluators that rely on trace input/output. For new code, set input/output on the root observation directly. See the [Python v3 → v4 migration guide](/docs/observability/sdk/upgrade-path/python-v3-to-v4).\\n \\n \\n```\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nfrom langfuse import get_client\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\nwith langfuse.start_as_current_observation(as_type=\\\"span\\\", name=\\\"complex-pipeline\\\") as root_span:\\n # Root span has its own input/output\\n root_span.update(input=\\\"Step 1 data\\\", output=\\\"Step 1 result\\\")\\n # But trace should have different input/output (e.g., for LLM-as-a-judge)\\n root_span.set_trace_io(\\n input={\\\"original_query\\\": \\\"User's actual question\\\"},\\n output={\\\"final_answer\\\": \\\"Complete response\\\", \\\"confidence\\\": 0.95}\\n )\\n # Now trace input/output are independent of root span input/output\\n///# Using the observe decorator\\n@observe()\\ndef process_user_query(user_question: str):\\n # LLM processing...\\n answer = call_llm(user_question)\\n # Explicitly set trace input/output for evaluation features\\n langfuse.set_current_trace_io(\\n input={\\\"question\\\": user_question},\\n output={\\\"answer\\\": answer}\\n )\\n return answer\\n```\\nUse [`propagateAttributes`](https://langfuse-js-git-main-langfuse.vercel.app/functions/_langfuse_tracing.propagateAttributes.html) to set correlating trace attributes, and [`setTraceIO`](https://langfuse-js-git-main-langfuse.vercel.app/classes/_langfuse_tracing.LangfuseSpan.html#settraceio) for trace-level input/output.\\n`.setTraceIO()` is deprecated and exists only for backward compatibility with trace-level LLM-as-a-judge evaluators. See the [JS/TS v4 → v5 migration guide](/docs/observability/sdk/upgrade-path/js-v4-to-v5).\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { propagateAttributes, startObservation } from \\\"@langfuse/tracing\\\";\\nconst userId = \\\"user-123\\\";\\nconst sessionId = \\\"session-abc\\\";\\npropagateAttributes(\\n {\\n userId: userId,\\n sessionId: sessionId,\\n tags: [\\\"authenticated-user\\\"],\\n metadata: { plan: \\\"premium\\\" },\\n },\\n () => {\\n const rootSpan = startObservation(\\\"data-processing\\\");\\n const generation = rootSpan.startObservation(\\n \\\"llm-call\\\",\\n {},\\n { asType: \\\"generation\\\" }\\n );\\n generation.end();\\n rootSpan.end();\\n }\\n);\\n```\\n## Trace and observation IDs\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n observation_id = langfuse.get_current_observation_id()\\n print(trace_id, observation_id)\\n```\\nUse [`createTraceId`](https://langfuse-js-git-main-langfuse.vercel.app/functions/_langfuse_tracing.createTraceId.html) to generate a deterministic trace ID from a seed.\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { createTraceId, startObservation } from \\\"@langfuse/tracing\\\";\\nconst externalId = \\\"support-ticket-54321\\\";\\nconst langfuseTraceId = await createTraceId(externalId);\\nconst rootSpan = startObservation(\\n \\\"process-ticket\\\",\\n {},\\n {\\n parentSpanContext: {\\n traceId: langfuseTraceId,\\n spanId: \\\"0123456789abcdef\\\",\\n traceFlags: 1,\\n },\\n }\\n);\\n```\\nUse [`getActiveTraceId`](https://langfuse-js-git-main-langfuse.vercel.app/functions/_langfuse_tracing.getActiveTraceId.html) to get the active trace ID and [`getActiveSpanId`](https://langfuse-js-git-main-langfuse.vercel.app/functions/_langfuse_tracing.getActiveSpanId.html) to get the current observation ID.\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { startObservation, getActiveTraceId } from \\\"@langfuse/tracing\\\";\\nawait startObservation(\\\"run\\\", async (span) => {\\n const traceId = getActiveTraceId();\\n console.log(`Current trace ID: ${traceId}`);\\n});\\n```\\n**Link to existing traces**\\nWhen integrating with upstream services that already have trace IDs, supply the W3C trace context so Langfuse spans join the existing tree rather than creating a new one.\\nPython SDKJS/TS SDK\\nUse the `trace_context` parameter to set custom trace context information.\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\nexisting_trace_id = \\\"abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890\\\"\\nexisting_parent_span_id = \\\"fedcba0987654321\\\"\\nwith langfuse.start_as_current_observation(\\n as_type=\\\"span\\\",\\n name=\\\"process-downstream-task\\\",\\n trace_context={\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n \\\"trace_id\\\": existing_trace_id,\\n \\\"parent_span_id\\\": existing_parent_span_id,\\n },\\n):\\n pass\\n```\\nUse the `parentSpanContext` parameter to set custom trace context information.\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { startObservation } from \\\"@langfuse/tracing\\\";\\nconst span = startObservation(\\n \\\"downstream-task\\\",\\n {},\\n {\\n parentSpanContext: {\\n traceId: \\\"abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890\\\",\\n spanId: \\\"fedcba0987654321\\\",\\n traceFlags: 1,\\n },\\n }\\n);\\nspan.end();\\n```\\n## Client lifecycle & flushing\\nAs the Langfuse SDKs are [asynchronous](/docs/observability/data-model#background-processing), they buffer spans in the background. Always [`flush()`](https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse#Langfuse.flush) or [`shutdown()`](https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse#Langfuse.shutdown) the client in short-lived processes (scripts, serverless functions, workers) to avoid losing data.\\nPython SDKJS/TS SDK\\n **[`flush()`](https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse#Langfuse.flush)**\\nManually triggers the sending of all buffered observations (spans, generations, scores, media metadata) to the Langfuse API. This is useful in short-lived scripts or before exiting an application to ensure all data is persisted.\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\n///# ... create traces and observations ...\\nlangfuse.flush() ///# Ensures all pending data is sent\\n```\\nThe `flush()` method blocks until the queued data is processed by the respective background threads.\\n **[`shutdown()`](https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse#Langfuse.shutdown)**\\nGracefully shuts down the Langfuse client. This includes:\\n 1. Flushing all buffered data (similar to `flush()`).\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n 2. Waiting for background threads (for data ingestion and media uploads) to finish their current tasks and terminate.\\nIt's crucial to call `shutdown()` before your application exits to prevent data loss and ensure clean resource release. The SDK automatically registers an `atexit` hook to call `shutdown()` on normal program termination, but manual invocation is recommended in scenarios like:\\n * Long-running daemons or services when they receive a shutdown signal.\\n * Applications where `atexit` might not reliably trigger (e.g., certain serverless environments or forceful terminations).\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\n///# ... application logic ...\\n///# Before exiting:\\nlangfuse.shutdown()\\n```\\nGeneric Serverless functionVercel Cloud Functions\\nExport the processor from your OTEL SDK setup file in order to call [`forceFlush()`](https://langfuse-js-git-main-langfuse.vercel.app/classes/_langfuse_otel.LangfuseSpanProcessor.html#forceflush) later.\\ninstrumentation.ts\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { NodeSDK } from \\\"@opentelemetry/sdk-node\\\";\\nimport { LangfuseSpanProcessor } from \\\"@langfuse/otel\\\";\\n// Export the processor to be able to flush it\\nexport const langfuseSpanProcessor = new LangfuseSpanProcessor({\\n exportMode: \\\"immediate\\\" // optional: configure immediate span export in serverless environments\\n});\\nconst sdk = new NodeSDK({\\n spanProcessors: [langfuseSpanProcessor],\\n});\\nsdk.start();\\n```\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/sdk/instrumentation\", \"title\": \"Instrumentation\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"## Trace and observation IDs\\nLangfuse follows the [W3C Trace Context standard](https://www.w3.org/TR/trace-context/):\\n * trace IDs are 32-character lowercase hex strings (16 bytes)\\n * observation IDs are 16-character lowercase hex strings (8 bytes)\\nYou cannot set arbitrary observation IDs, but you can generate deterministic trace IDs to correlate with external systems.\\nSee [Trace IDs & Distributed Tracing](/docs/observability/features/trace-ids-and-distributed-tracing) for more information on correlating traces across services.\\nPython SDKJS/TS SDK\\nUse [`create_trace_id()`](https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse#Langfuse.create_trace_id) to generate a trace ID. If a `seed` is provided, the ID is deterministic. Use the same seed to get the same ID. This is useful for correlating external IDs with Langfuse traces.\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client, Langfuse\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\nexternal_request_id = \\\"req_12345\\\"\\ndeterministic_trace_id = langfuse.create_trace_id(seed=external_request_id)\\n```\\nUse [`get_current_trace_id()`](https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse#Langfuse.get_current_trace_id) to get the current trace ID and [`get_current_observation_id`](https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse#Langfuse.get_current_observation_id) to get the current observation ID.\\nYou can also use `observation.trace_id` and `observation.id` to access the trace and observation IDs directly from a LangfuseSpan or LangfuseGeneration object.\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client, Langfuse\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\nwith langfuse.start_as_current_observation(as_type=\\\"span\\\", name=\\\"my-op\\\") as current_op:\\n trace_id = langfuse.get_current_trace_id()\\n observation_id = langfuse.get_current_observation_id()\\n print(trace_id, observation_id)\\n```\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/sdk/overview\", \"title\": \"Langfuse SDKs\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Overview - Langfuse\\n[Docs](/docs)\\n[Observability](/docs/observability/overview)\\n[SDKs](/docs/observability/sdk/overview)\\n[Overview](/docs/observability/sdk/overview)\\n# Langfuse SDKs\\nLangfuse offers two SDKs:\\n * **Python SDK v4** [](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse-python) [](https://pypi.org/project/langfuse/)\\n * **JS/TS SDK v5** [](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse-js) [](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@langfuse/tracing)\\n * **Other Languages** via OpenTelemetry\\nThe Langfuse SDKs are the recommended way to create [custom observations and traces](/docs/observability/sdk/instrumentation#custom-instrumentation) and use the Langfuse [prompt-management](/docs/prompt-management/overview) and [evaluation](/docs/evaluation/overview) features.\\n**Key benefits**\\n * Based on [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/), so you can use any OTEL-based instrumentation library for your LLM stack.\\n * Fully [async requests](/docs/observability/data-model#background-processing), meaning Langfuse adds almost no latency.\\n * Interoperable with Langfuse [native integrations](/integrations).\\n * Accurate latency tracking via synchronous timestamps.\\n * IDs available for downstream use.\\n * Great DX when nesting observations.\\n * Cannot break your application: SDK errors are caught and logged.\\nThis section documents tracing related features of the Langfuse SDK. To use the Langfuse SDK for [prompt management](/docs/prompt-management/overview) and [evaluation](/docs/evaluation/overview), visit their respective documentation.\\nRequirements for self-hosted Langfuse\\n+\\nSDK| Minimum self-hosted server version| Notes \\n---|---|--- \\nPython SDK v3 and v4| [≥ 3.63.0](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/releases/tag/v3.63.0)| Observations API v2 and Metrics API v2 require Langfuse v4 \"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nJS/TS SDK v4 and v5| [≥ 3.63.0](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/releases/tag/v3.63.0)| Observations API v2 and Metrics API v2 require Langfuse v4 \\n \\nLangfuse Cloud always satisfies these minimums. See the [self-hosted compatibility matrix](/self-hosting/upgrade/versioning#sdk-server) for the full picture per server version, and [Versions & Compatibility](/docs/compatibility) for Langfuse Cloud.\\nLegacy documentation\\n+\\nThis documentation is for the latest versions of the Langfuse SDKs.\\n * Documentation for the legacy Python SDK v3 can be found [here](https://python-sdk-v3.docs-snapshot.langfuse.com/docs/observability/sdk/overview/).\\n * Documentation for the legacy TypeScript SDK v4 can be found [here](https://js-sdk-v4-docs-snapshot.langfuse.com/docs/observability/sdk/overview/).\\n## Quickstart\\nFollow the quickstart guide to get the first trace into Langfuse. See the setup section for more details.\\nPython SDKJS/TS SDK\\n **1\\\\. Install package:**\\n \\n \\n```\\npip install langfuse\\n```\\n**2\\\\. Add credentials:**\\n.env\\n \\n \\n```\\nLANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY = \\\"sk-lf-...\\\"\\nLANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY = \\\"pk-lf-...\\\"\\nLANGFUSE_BASE_URL = \\\"https://cloud.langfuse.com\\\" # 🇪🇺 EU region\\n///# Other Langfuse data regions include 🇺🇸 US: https://us.cloud.langfuse.com, 🇯🇵 Japan: https://jp.cloud.langfuse.com and ⚕️ HIPAA: https://hipaa.cloud.langfuse.com\\n```\\n**3\\\\. Instrument your application:**\\nInstrumentation means adding code that records what’s happening in your application so it can be sent to Langfuse. There are three main ways of instrumenting your code with the Python SDK.\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nIn this example we will use the [context manager](/docs/observability/sdk/instrumentation#context-manager). You can also use the [decorator](/docs/observability/sdk/instrumentation#observe-wrapper) or create [manual observations](/docs/observability/sdk/instrumentation#manual-observations).\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\n///# Create a span using a context manager\\nwith langfuse.start_as_current_observation(as_type=\\\"span\\\", name=\\\"process-request\\\") as span:\\n # Your processing logic here\\n span.update(output=\\\"Processing complete\\\")\\n # Create a nested generation for an LLM call\\n with langfuse.start_as_current_observation(as_type=\\\"generation\\\", name=\\\"llm-response\\\", model=\\\"gpt-3.5-turbo\\\") as generation:\\n # Your LLM call logic here\\n generation.update(output=\\\"Generated response\\\")\\n///# All spans are automatically closed when exiting their context blocks\\n///# Flush events in short-lived applications\\nlangfuse.flush()\\n```\\n_[When should I call`langfuse.flush()`?](/docs/observability/data-model#background-processing)_\\n**4\\\\. Run your application and see the trace in Langfuse:**\\nSee the [trace in Langfuse](https://cloud.langfuse.com/project/cloramnkj0002jz088vzn1ja4/traces/b8789d62464dc7627016d9748a48ad0d?observation=5c7c133ec919ded7&timestamp=2025-12-03T14:56:19.285Z).\\n **1\\\\. Install packages:**\\n \\n \\n```\\nnpm install @langfuse/tracing @langfuse/otel @opentelemetry/sdk-node\\n```\\n **2\\\\. Set environment variables:**\\n.env\\n \\n \\n```\\nLANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY = \\\"sk-lf-...\\\"\\nLANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY = \\\"pk-lf-...\\\"\\nLANGFUSE_BASE_URL = \\\"https://cloud.langfuse.com\\\" # 🇪🇺 EU region\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n///# Other Langfuse data regions include 🇺🇸 US: https://us.cloud.langfuse.com, 🇯🇵 Japan: https://jp.cloud.langfuse.com and ⚕️ HIPAA: https://hipaa.cloud.langfuse.com\\n```\\n **3\\\\. Initialize OpenTelemetry:**\\nCreate an `instrumentation.ts` to register the Langfuse span processor so traces reach Langfuse.\\ninstrumentation.ts\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { NodeSDK } from \\\"@opentelemetry/sdk-node\\\";\\nimport { LangfuseSpanProcessor } from \\\"@langfuse/otel\\\";\\nexport const sdk = new NodeSDK({\\n spanProcessors: [new LangfuseSpanProcessor()],\\n});\\nsdk.start();\\n```\\nImport this file at the top of your app's entry point (e.g., `index.ts`).\\n **4\\\\. Instrument your app:**\\nInstrumentation means adding code that records what’s happening in your application so it can be sent to Langfuse. There are three main ways of instrumenting your code with the TypeScript SDK.\\nIn this example we will use the [context manager](/docs/observability/sdk/instrumentation#context-manager). You can also use the [decorator](/docs/observability/sdk/instrumentation#observe-wrapper) or create [manual observations](/docs/observability/sdk/instrumentation#manual-observations).\\nindex.ts\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { sdk } from \\\"./instrumentation\\\";\\nimport { startActiveObservation } from \\\"@langfuse/tracing\\\";\\nasync function main() {\\n await startActiveObservation(\\\"my-first-trace\\\", async (span) => {\\n span.update({\\n input: \\\"Hello, Langfuse!\\\",\\n output: \\\"This is my first trace!\\\",\\n });\\n });\\n}\\n// Shutdown flushes events and is required for short-lived applications\\nmain().finally(() => sdk.shutdown());\\n```\\n _[When do I need to use`shutdown()`?](/docs/observability/data-model#background-processing)_\\n **5\\\\. Run your application and see the trace in Langfuse:**\\n \\n \\n```\\nnpx tsx index.ts\\n```\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n print(\\\"Authentication failed. Please check your credentials and host.\\\")\\n```\\nThe Langfuse client is a singleton. It can be accessed anywhere in your application using the [`get_client()`](https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse#get_client) function.\\nAlternative: Configure via constructor\\n+\\nOptionally, you can initialize the client via [`Langfuse()`](https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse#Langfuse) to pass in configuration options (see below). Otherwise, it is created automatically when you call [`get_client()`](https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse#get_client) based on environment variables.\\nIf you create multiple `Langfuse` instances with the same `public_key`, the singleton instance is reused and new arguments are ignored.\\nInitialize client\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import Langfuse\\nlangfuse = Langfuse(\\n public_key=\\\"your-public-key\\\",\\n secret_key=\\\"your-secret-key\\\",\\n base_url=\\\"https://cloud.langfuse.com\\\", ///# 🇪🇺 EU region\\n # Other Langfuse data regions include 🇺🇸 US: https://us.cloud.langfuse.com, 🇯🇵 Japan: https://jp.cloud.langfuse.com and ⚕️ HIPAA: https://hipaa.cloud.langfuse.com\\n)\\n```\\nAll key configuration options are listed in the [Python SDK reference](https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse#Langfuse).\\nInitialize the [`LangfuseClient`](https://langfuse-js-git-main-langfuse.vercel.app/classes/_langfuse_client.LangfuseClient.html) to interact with Langfuse. The client will automatically use the environment variables you set above.\\nclient.ts\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { LangfuseClient } from \\\"@langfuse/client\\\";\\nconst langfuse = new LangfuseClient();\\n```\\nAlternative: Configure via constructor\\n+\\nYou can also pass the Langfuse credentials directly to the constructor:\\nclient.ts\\n \"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n \\n```\\nimport { LangfuseClient } from \\\"@langfuse/client\\\";\\nconst langfuse = new LangfuseClient({\\n publicKey: \\\"your-public-key\\\",\\n secretKey: \\\"your-secret-key\\\",\\n baseUrl: \\\"https://cloud.langfuse.com\\\", // or your self-hosted instance\\n});\\n```\\n### Use the SDK\\nWith the SDK set up, you can:\\n * [Instrument your application](/docs/observability/sdk/instrumentation#custom-observations)\\n * Use [Langfuse Prompt Management](/docs/prompt-management/get-started)\\n * Run [Experiments](/docs/evaluation/experiments/experiments-via-sdk) and create [Scores](/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/custom-scores)\\n * [Query data](/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/query-via-sdk)\\n## OpenTelemetry foundation\\nThe Langfuse SDKs are built on top of [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/). This provides:\\n * **Standardization** with the wider observability ecosystem and tooling.\\n * **Robust context propagation** so nested spans stay connected, even across async workloads.\\n * **Attribute propagation** to keep `userId`, `sessionId`, `metadata`, `version`, and `tags` aligned across observations.\\n * **Ecosystem interoperability** meaning third-party instrumentations automatically appear inside Langfuse traces.\\nThe following diagram shows how Langfuse maps to native OpenTelemetry concepts:\\nLangfuse\\nOpenTelemetry\\nis defined by\\nHierarchy via \\nContext Propagation\\nCollects one or more\\nshares ID with\\nMapped to\\nMapped to\\nsets default input and output\\ncan hold trace attributes\\ncan hold trace attributes\\nOTel Trace\\nRoot OTel Span\\nChild OTel Span\\nLangfuse Trace\\nLangfuse Observation \\n(typed as either Span, Generation or Event)\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n * [**Attribute Propagation**](/docs/observability/sdk/instrumentation#add-attributes): Certain trace attributes (`user_id`, `session_id`, `metadata`, `version`, `tags`, and request-scoped `environment` in the Python SDK) can be automatically propagated to all child observations using `propagate_attributes()`. This ensures consistent attribute coverage across all observations in a trace. See the [instrumentation docs](/docs/observability/sdk/python/instrumentation#propagating-trace-attributes) for details.\\nThe Langfuse SDKs provide wrappers around OTel spans ([`LangfuseSpan`](https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse#LangfuseSpan), [`LangfuseGeneration`](https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse#LangfuseGeneration)) that offer convenient methods for interacting with Langfuse-specific features like scoring and media handling, while still being native OTel spans under the hood. You can also use these wrapper objects to add Langfuse trace attributes via [`update_trace()`](https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse#LangfuseEvent.update) or use [`propagate_attributes()`](https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse#propagate_attributes) for automatic propagation to all child observations.\\n## Learn more\\n[\\n### Instrument your app\\n](/docs/observability/sdk/instrumentation)\\n[\\n### Advanced features\\n](/docs/observability/sdk/advanced-features)\\n[\\n### Upgrade path\\n](/docs/observability/sdk/upgrade-path)\\n[\\n### Troubleshooting & FAQ\\n](/docs/observability/sdk/troubleshooting-and-faq)\\n[\\n### Python API reference\\n](https://python.reference.langfuse.com)\\n[\\n### JS/TS API reference\\n](https://js.reference.langfuse.com/)\\n## Other languages\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nLangfuse maintains SDKs for Python and JavaScript/TypeScript. For other languages, you can use our [OpenTelemetry endpoint](/integrations/native/opentelemetry) to instrument your application and use the [public API](/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/public-api) to use Langfuse prompt management, evaluation, and querying.\\n### Instrumentation\\nTo instrument your application, you can send OpenTelemetry spans to the [Langfuse OTel endpoint](/integrations/native/opentelemetry). For this, you can use the following OpenTelemetry SDKs:\\n * [JetBrains Tracy for Kotlin/Java](https://github.com/JetBrains/tracy)\\n * [OpenTelemetry Java](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/languages/java/)\\n * [OpenTelemetry .NET](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/languages/net/)\\n * [OpenTelemetry Go](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/languages/go/)\\n * [OpenTelemetry C++](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/languages/cpp/)\\n * [OpenTelemetry Erlang/Elixir](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/languages/erlang/)\\n * [OpenTelemetry Ruby](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/languages/ruby/)\\n * [OpenTelemetry PHP](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/languages/php/)\\n * [OpenTelemetry Rust](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/languages/rust/)\\n * [OpenTelemetry Swift](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/languages/swift/)\\n### Prompt management, evaluation, and querying:\\nTo use other Langfuse features, you can use the [public API](/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/public-api) to integrate Langfuse from any runtime. We also provide a list of community-maintained SDKs [here](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse-examples?tab=readme-ov-file#community-maintained-sdks).\\n* * *\\n* * *\\nLast edited 7/31/2026\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"site\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/changelog/2025-06-05-python-sdk-v3-generally-available\", \"title\": \"Python SDK v3 is now Generally Available - Langfuse\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n langfuse.update_current_trace(user_id=user_id, tags=[\\\"experimental\\\"])\\n\\n\\n \\n # Call a function from another module\\n\\n\\n processed_data = other_module.process_data(user_query)\\n\\n\\n \\n # Update the root span\\n\\n\\n langfuse.update_current_span(output={\\\"final_result\\\": processed_data})\\n\\n\\n return processed_data\\n\\n\\n \\n\\n\\nhandle_user_request(\\\"Tell me a joke about OpenTelemetry\\\", \\\"user_123\\\")\\n\\n\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n \\n \\n```\\n\\n\\n///# other_module.py\\nfrom langfuse import get_client, observe\\n \\n///# Access the initialized Langfuse client globally\\n///# If no client is initialized, it will be initialized with the default configuration\\n///# from the environment variables\\n\\n\\nlangfuse_client = get_client()\\n\\n\\n \\n\\n\\n@observe(name=\\\"data-processing-step\\\")\\n\\n\\ndef process_data(query: str):\\n\\n\\n # This span is automatically a child of \\\"user-request-pipeline\\\".\\n \\n\\n\\n with langfuse_client.start_as_current_generation(\\n\\n\\n name=\\\"joke-generation-llm\\\",\\n\\n\\n model=\\\"gpt-4o\\\",\\n\\n\\n input=[{\\\"role\\\": \\\"user\\\", \\\"content\\\": query}]\\n\\n\\n ) as generation:\\n\\n\\n # Simulate LLM call\\n\\n\\n joke = \\\"Why did the OpenTelemetry collector break up with the span? It needed more space for its attributes!\\\"\\n\\n\\n generation.update(output=joke, usage_details={\\\"input_tokens\\\": 10, \\\"output_tokens\\\": 25})\\n\\n\\n \\n\\n\\n return joke\\n\\n\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\nIn this example:\\n\\n---\\n\\n * Langfuse resources are initialized once under the hood by the `get_client()` function. It can be accessed globally via `langfuse = get_client()`.\\n\\n---\\n\\n * The `@observe` decorator creates spans for `handle_user_request` and `process_data`.\\n\\n---\\n\\n * `other_module.py` accesses the same client instance via `get_client()`.\\n\\n---\\n\\n * Spans are automatically nested due to OTEL’s context propagation.\\n * Trace and span updates can be done contextually.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Seamless third-party integrations\\n\\n---\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/sdk/advanced-features\", \"title\": \"Advanced features\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Advanced Features - Langfuse\\n[Docs](/docs)\\n[Observability](/docs/observability/overview)\\n[SDKs](/docs/observability/sdk/overview)\\n[Advanced Features](/docs/observability/sdk/advanced-features)\\n# Advanced features\\nUse these methods to harden your Langfuse instrumentation, protect sensitive data, and adapt the SDKs to your specific environment.\\n## Filtering by Instrumentation Scope\\nLangfuse now applies a **default span filter** in both SDKs to keep exports LLM-focused without extra configuration.\\nBy default, a span is exported if **any** of these are true:\\n * It was created by the Langfuse SDK (`instrumentation_scope.name == \\\"langfuse-sdk\\\"`)\\n * It has at least one `gen_ai.*` attribute\\n * It comes from a known LLM instrumentation scope (for example `openinference.*`, `langsmith`, `haystack`, `litellm`, `agent_framework`, `strands-agents`, `vllm`, `opentelemetry.instrumentation.anthropic`)\\nIf you want another integration added to the default instrumentation scope allowlist, open an issue in [langfuse/langfuse](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/issues) with the scope name and a sample span.\\nYou can inspect a span's instrumentation scope in Langfuse under `metadata.scope.name`. Filtered-out spans do not appear in the UI.\\nTo identify filtered scopes:\\n 1. Enable debug logging (`Langfuse(debug=True)` or `LANGFUSE_DEBUG=\\\"True\\\"` on Python, `LANGFUSE_DEBUG=\\\"true\\\"` or `LANGFUSE_LOG_LEVEL=\\\"DEBUG\\\"` on JS/TS).\\n 2. Run your application and check logs for dropped-span messages and instrumentation scope names.\\n 3. Add those scopes to your allowlist logic by composing with `is_default_export_span` / `isDefaultExportSpan`.\\n 4. Optional: temporarily use `should_export_span=lambda span: True` or `shouldExportSpan: () => true` to inspect all spans, then restore filtering.\\nBehavior Change\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nFor all integrations in multi-project setups, you must specify the `public_key` parameter to ensure traces are routed to the correct project.\\n **Observe Decorator:**\\nPass `langfuse_public_key` as a keyword argument to the _top-most_ observed function (not the decorator). From Python SDK >= 3.2.2, nested decorated functions will automatically pick up the public key from the execution context they are currently into. Also, calls to `get_client` will be also aware of the current `langfuse_public_key` in the decorated function execution context, so passing the `langfuse_public_key` here again is not necessary.\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import observe\\n@observe\\ndef nested():\\n # get_client call is context aware\\n # if it runs inside another decorated function that has\\n # langfuse_public_key passed, it does not need passing here again\\n@observe\\ndef process_data_for_project_a(data):\\n # passing `langfuse_public_key` here again is not necessarily\\n # as it is stored in execution context\\n nested()\\n return {\\\"processed\\\": data}\\n@observe\\ndef process_data_for_project_b(data):\\n # passing `langfuse_public_key` here again is not necessarily\\n # as it is stored in execution context\\n nested()\\n return {\\\"enhanced\\\": data}\\n///# Route to Project A\\n///# Top-most decorated function needs `langfuse_public_key` kwarg\\nresult_a = process_data_for_project_a(\\n data=\\\"input data\\\",\\n langfuse_public_key=\\\"pk-lf-project-a-...\\\"\\n)\\n///# Route to Project B\\n///# Top-most decorated function needs `langfuse_public_key` kwarg\\nresult_b = process_data_for_project_b(\\n data=\\\"input data\\\",\\n langfuse_public_key=\\\"pk-lf-project-b-...\\\"\\n)\\n```\\n **OpenAI Integration:**\\nAdd `langfuse_public_key` as a keyword argument to the OpenAI execution:\\n \"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse.openai import openai\\nclient = openai.OpenAI()\\n///# Route to Project A\\nresponse_a = client.chat.completions.create(\\n model=\\\"gpt-4o\\\",\\n messages=[{\\\"role\\\": \\\"user\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"Hello from Project A\\\"}],\\n langfuse_public_key=\\\"pk-lf-project-a-...\\\"\\n)\\n///# Route to Project B\\nresponse_b = client.chat.completions.create(\\n model=\\\"gpt-4o\\\",\\n messages=[{\\\"role\\\": \\\"user\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"Hello from Project B\\\"}],\\n langfuse_public_key=\\\"pk-lf-project-b-...\\\"\\n)\\n```\\n **Langchain Integration:**\\nAdd `public_key` to the CallbackHandler constructor:\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse.langchain import CallbackHandler\\nfrom langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI\\nfrom langchain_core.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate\\n///# Create handlers for different projects\\nhandler_a = CallbackHandler(public_key=\\\"pk-lf-project-a-...\\\")\\nhandler_b = CallbackHandler(public_key=\\\"pk-lf-project-b-...\\\")\\nllm = ChatOpenAI(model_name=\\\"gpt-4o\\\")\\nprompt = ChatPromptTemplate.from_template(\\\"Tell me about {topic}\\\")\\nchain = prompt | llm\\n///# Route to Project A\\nresponse_a = chain.invoke(\\n {\\\"topic\\\": \\\"machine learning\\\"},\\n config={\\\"callbacks\\\": [handler_a]}\\n)\\n///# Route to Project B\\nresponse_b = chain.invoke(\\n {\\\"topic\\\": \\\"data science\\\"},\\n config={\\\"callbacks\\\": [handler_b]}\\n)\\n```\\n **Important Considerations:**\\n * Every Langfuse SDK execution across all integrations must include the appropriate public key parameter\\n * Missing public key parameters may result in traces being routed to the default project or lost\\n * Third-party OpenTelemetry spans that pass filtering may appear in all projects since they lack the Langfuse public key attribute\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nYou can configure the SDK to send traces to multiple Langfuse projects. This is useful for multi-tenant applications or for sending traces to different environments. Simply register multiple `LangfuseSpanProcessor` instances, each with its own credentials.\\ninstrumentation.ts\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { NodeSDK } from \\\"@opentelemetry/sdk-node\\\";\\nimport { LangfuseSpanProcessor } from \\\"@langfuse/otel\\\";\\nconst sdk = new NodeSDK({\\n spanProcessors: [\\n new LangfuseSpanProcessor({\\n publicKey: \\\"pk-lf-public-key-project-1\\\",\\n secretKey: \\\"sk-lf-secret-key-project-1\\\",\\n }),\\n new LangfuseSpanProcessor({\\n publicKey: \\\"pk-lf-public-key-project-2\\\",\\n secretKey: \\\"sk-lf-secret-key-project-2\\\",\\n }),\\n ],\\n});\\nsdk.start();\\n```\\nThis configuration sends every span accepted by each processor's filter to both projects. You can configure a custom `shouldExportSpan` filter for each processor to control which traces go to which project.\\n## Time to first token (TTFT)\\nYou can manually set the time to first token (TTFT) of your LLM calls. This is useful for measuring the latency of your LLM calls and for identifying slow LLM calls.\\nPython SDKJS/TS SDK\\nYou can use the `completion_start_time` attribute to manually set the time to first token (TTFT) of your LLM calls. This is useful for measuring the latency of your LLM calls and for identifying slow LLM calls.\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client\\nimport datetime, time\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\nwith langfuse.start_as_current_observation(as_type=\\\"generation\\\", name=\\\"TTFT-Generation\\\") as generation:\\n time.sleep(3)\\n generation.update(\\n completion_start_time=datetime.datetime.now(),\\n output=\\\"some response\\\",\\n )\\nlangfuse.flush()\\n```\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nUse the OpenTelemetry threading instrumentor so context flows across worker threads.\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom opentelemetry.instrumentation.threading import ThreadingInstrumentor\\nThreadingInstrumentor().instrument()\\n```\\nFor multiprocessing, follow the [OpenTelemetry guidance](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/issues/2765#issuecomment-1158402076). If you use Pydantic Logfire, enable `distributed_tracing=True`. For tracing across separate services or processes, see [Trace IDs & Distributed Tracing](/docs/observability/features/trace-ids-and-distributed-tracing).\\n* * *\\n* * *\\nLast edited 6/16/2026\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/guides/cookbook/example_data_migration\", \"title\": \"Migrating Data Between Langfuse Projects (Python SDK v4)\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n%pip install --quiet \\\"langfuse>=4.8.1\\\" \\\"opentelemetry-sdk>=1.25.0\\\" \\\"opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http>=1.25.0\\\"\\n```\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport os\\n///# --- SOURCE project credentials \\n\\nos.environ.setdefault(\\\"LANGFUSE_SOURCE_PUBLIC_KEY\\\", \\\"pk-lf-..\\\");\\nos.environ.setdefault(\\\"LANGFUSE_SOURCE_SECRET_KEY\\\", \\\"sk-lf-...\\\");\\nos.environ.setdefault(\\\"LANGFUSE_SOURCE_HOST\\\", \\\"https://cloud.langfuse.com\\\"); ///# e.g. EU cloud\\n///# --- DESTINATION project credentials \\n\\nos.environ.setdefault(\\\"LANGFUSE_DEST_PUBLIC_KEY\\\", \\\"pk-lf-..\\\");\\nos.environ.setdefault(\\\"LANGFUSE_DEST_SECRET_KEY\\\", \\\"sk-lf-...\\\");\\nos.environ.setdefault(\\\"LANGFUSE_DEST_HOST\\\", \\\"https://hipaa.cloud.langfuse.com\\\"); ///# e.g. HIPAA cloud\\n///# --- Optional time filter for the observations migration (ISO 8601) \\n\\n///# Leave empty to migrate all traces.\\nos.environ.setdefault(\\\"LANGFUSE_MIGRATE_FROM_TIMESTAMP\\\", \\\"2026-03-01T00:00:00Z\\\"); ///# e.g. \\\"2025-01-01T00:00:00Z\\\"\\nos.environ.setdefault(\\\"LANGFUSE_MIGRATE_TO_TIMESTAMP\\\", \\\"2026-04-20T00:00:00Z\\\"); ///# e.g. \\\"2025-02-01T00:00:00Z\\\"\\n```\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport base64\\nimport datetime as dt\\nimport json\\nimport re\\nimport time\\nfrom hashlib import sha256\\nfrom typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional\\nfrom langfuse import Langfuse\\nSOURCE_CFG = {\\n \\\"public_key\\\": os.environ[\\\"LANGFUSE_SOURCE_PUBLIC_KEY\\\"],\\n \\\"secret_key\\\": os.environ[\\\"LANGFUSE_SOURCE_SECRET_KEY\\\"],\\n \\\"base_url\\\": os.environ.get(\\\"LANGFUSE_SOURCE_HOST\\\", \\\"https://cloud.langfuse.com\\\").rstrip(\\\"/\\\"),\\n}\\nDEST_CFG = {\\n \\\"public_key\\\": os.environ[\\\"LANGFUSE_DEST_PUBLIC_KEY\\\"],\\n \\\"secret_key\\\": os.environ[\\\"LANGFUSE_DEST_SECRET_KEY\\\"],\\n \\\"base_url\\\": os.environ.get(\\\"LANGFUSE_DEST_HOST\\\", \\\"https://cloud.langfuse.com\\\").rstrip(\\\"/\\\"),\\n}\\n///# Sanity: source and destination must use different public keys. The Langfuse v4\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n trace_name = getattr(trace_obj, \\\"trace_name\\\", None) or trace_obj.name\\n _set_scalar(span, \\\"langfuse.trace.name\\\", trace_name)\\n _set_scalar(span, \\\"langfuse.user.id\\\", trace_obj.user_id)\\n _set_scalar(span, \\\"langfuse.session.id\\\", trace_obj.session_id)\\n _set_scalar(span, \\\"langfuse.release\\\", getattr(trace_obj, \\\"release\\\", None))\\n _set_scalar(span, \\\"langfuse.version\\\", trace_obj.version)\\n _set_scalar(span, \\\"langfuse.environment\\\", trace_obj.environment or \\\"default\\\")\\n if trace_obj.public is not None:\\n span.set_attribute(\\\"langfuse.trace.public\\\", bool(trace_obj.public))\\n if getattr(trace_obj, \\\"tags\\\", None):\\n # Langfuse accepts both a string[] attribute and a JSON string.\\n span.set_attribute(\\\"langfuse.trace.tags\\\", list(trace_obj.tags))\\n input_str = _as_attr_string(trace_obj.input)\\n if input_str is not None:\\n span.set_attribute(\\\"langfuse.observation.input\\\", input_str)\\n output_str = _as_attr_string(trace_obj.output)\\n if output_str is not None:\\n span.set_attribute(\\\"langfuse.observation.output\\\", output_str)\\n md = trace_obj.metadata\\n if isinstance(md, dict):\\n for k, v in md.items():\\n _set_scalar(span, Great! Here are minimal, runnable examples to get your first trace into Langfuse.

Python (SDK v4)

  • Install: pip install langfuse

  • Set env (e.g., .env): LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-... LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-... LANGFUSE_BASE_URL=https://cloud.langfuse.com

  • Code: from langfuse import get_client

    langfuse = get_client()

    with langfuse.start_as_current_observation(as_type="span", name="process-request") as span: span.update(output="Processing complete") with langfuse.start_as_current_observation( as_type="generation", name="llm-response", model="gpt-3.5-turbo" ) as gen: gen.update(output="Generated response")

    langfuse.flush() # important for short-lived scripts

Docs:

  • SDK Quickstart (Python): https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/sdk/overview
  • Instrumentation: https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/sdk/instrumentation

JavaScript/TypeScript (SDK v5)

  • Install: npm install @langfuse/tracing @langfuse/otel @opentelemetry/sdk-node

  • Set env (e.g., .env): LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-... LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-... LANGFUSE_BASE_URL=https://cloud.langfuse.com

  • instrumentation.ts: import { NodeSDK } from "@opentelemetry/sdk-node"; import { LangfuseSpanProcessor } from "@langfuse/otel";

    export const sdk = new NodeSDK({ spanProcessors: [new LangfuseSpanProcessor()], }); sdk.start();

  • index.ts: import { sdk } from "./instrumentation"; import { startActiveObservation } from "@langfuse/tracing";

    async function main() { await startActiveObservation("my-first-trace", async (span) => { span.update({ input: "Hello, Langfuse!", output: "This is my first trace!" }); }); }

    main().finally(() => sdk.shutdown()); // flush in short-lived apps

Docs:

  • SDK Quickstart (JS/TS): https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/sdk/overview#quickstart
  • Instrumentation: https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/sdk/instrumentation
